rows.draftLearningTask: Use simulated malaria cases to connect parasite biology with presentation, complications and management priorities.
Write a simulated malaria prescription and justify it using species, local resistance and current national guidance.
Distinguish major forms of leishmaniasis and relate their presentation and management to the underlying infection.
Relate filarial transmission and pathology to acute and chronic presentations and outline management goals.
Explain how cysticercosis develops and use lesion location and complications to reason through a simulated management plan.
Explain an identified infection and its treatment to a simulated patient and family and check understanding.
Counsel a simulated household on feasible ways to reduce infection risks from its environment.
Interpret Indian TB epidemiology and explain the impact of the disease on households, work and the economy.
Trace TB transmission and progression and contrast pulmonary disease with nodal, skeletal and CNS presentations.
Explain how HIV and diabetes can alter the course and presentation of TB.
Distinguish transmission of resistant TB from resistance acquired during treatment and identify contributing factors.
Elicit, document and present a focused TB history that includes exposure, constitutional symptoms and possible extrapulmonary involvement.
Perform a focused examination in a simulated TB case and adapt chest, lymph node and neurologic assessment to the presentation.
Interpret example tuberculin skin test findings and explain when the test is useful and what limits interpretation.
Present and defend a ranked differential diagnosis in a simulated patient with suspected pulmonary or extrapulmonary TB.
Select and interpret investigations for a simulated TB case using imaging, microbiology, HIV testing and site-specific specimens as indicated.
Interpret supplied sputum Gram stain, acid-fast microscopy and susceptibility reports and explain what each can establish.
Explain when molecular testing, specialized culture and drug susceptibility testing can answer a TB diagnostic question and discuss limitations of serology.
Explain the rationale, indications, administration technique, benefits and possible adverse effects of BCG vaccination.
Compare anti-TB agents by indication, contraindications, interactions and adverse effects in case examples.
Write and defend a simulated TB prescription using current national guidance, disease site, microbiology and comorbidities, and explain treatment support.
Use exposure scenarios to explain TB precautions, contact screening, testing and eligibility for preventive treatment.
Apply programme outcome definitions to TB follow-up examples and explain how resistance is recognized, prevented and managed.
Brief simulated healthcare workers on the national TB programme and demonstrate how to support and monitor treatment.
Explain TB diagnosis and treatment to a simulated patient and family, respond to concerns and confirm understanding.
Define obstructive airway disease and classify representative conditions by their pattern of airflow limitation.
Explain how population risk factors and disease progression shape the burden of obstructive airway disease.
Identify likely triggers of acute deterioration in obstructive airway disease from short clinical scenarios.
Use sample gas exchange findings to explain mechanisms of hypoxaemia and hypercapnia.
Explain how inherited alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency predisposes to emphysema and when family history is informative.
Distinguish environmental exposures that contribute to chronic airway disease from those that worsen symptoms.
Compare allergic and non-allergic triggers using patient histories and explain how they shape the assessment.
Elicit and present a respiratory history that differentiates likely causes, severity and triggers of airway obstruction.
Examine a simulated breathless patient, assess respiratory distress and identify findings suggesting consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax.
Present a ranked differential for suspected airway obstruction and defend it using distinguishing clinical features.
Interpret sample pulmonary function tests and explain how test quality and airflow patterns affect the conclusion.
Demonstrate peak expiratory flow measurement, record the result and interpret it in context.
Present a targeted investigation plan for a simulated patient with airway obstruction and justify it against the leading diagnosis.
Explain when to use pulse oximetry, arterial blood gases and chest radiography and interpret example results together.
Compare pharmacologic and supportive therapies for obstructive airway disease by indication, expected benefit and limitations.
Explain how age, risk factors and clinical context inform vaccination decisions in obstructive airway disease.
Present and defend a simulated maintenance plan for obstructive airway disease, including appropriate use of bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids.
Present a simulated exacerbation plan and justify the roles of bronchodilators, systemic steroids and antimicrobials when indicated.
Compare indications, monitoring and safety considerations for hospital and home oxygen therapy.
Use a role-play to assess readiness to quit smoking and agree on a feasible cessation and follow-up plan.
Demonstrate device-specific inhaler technique and use return demonstration to identify and correct errors.
Explain the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up plan to a simulated patient and check their understanding.
Explain how obstructive airway disease affects daily function, wellbeing, family responsibilities and employment.
Propose workplace exposure controls for a simulated setting and explain how they could reduce respiratory risk.
Respond empathetically to a simulated patient with limited control over work or housing exposures and agree on feasible changes.
Explore barriers to smoking cessation in a role-play and respond to relapse or ambivalence without blame.
